source_review.notes: Checked current Arrow, DuckDB, DataFusion, Spark, ORC, Parquet, and Velox columnar/vector/interface/operator documentation plus primary Dremel and F1 Query sources. Twelve initial URLs returned HTTP 200; one obsolete singular Velox vector URL was excluded and replaced by its current plural-path page, leaving all thirteen final citations at HTTP 200. Product behavior is attributed and performance guidance states its assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed batch schema, length, field vectors, selection set, validity, encoding, typed kernel, architecture, and semantic function.
Reviewed setup/value/decode costs, active cardinality, and complete peak-memory components.
Checked nonnegative lengths, in-range positions, set inclusion, units, bounds, and conditional equivalence.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical length, active cardinality, encoded bytes, decoded bytes, live memory, and useful output remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced batch_size=5, selected_positions=(2,4), and projected_values=(16,20).
Verified invalid position 1 with placeholder 999 is excluded before projection.
Recomputed the compression example's four frames as potentially 1.6 GiB decoded before other receiver state.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture demonstrates validity and selection semantics only, not SIMD or cluster performance.

evidence: Verified filtering selection correctness requires exactly positions whose predicate evaluates true; false and unknown are excluded.
Verified batch-partition invariance needs correct state across boundaries and declared handling of order, volatility, errors, and effects.
Verified zero-copy needs layout compatibility and retained ownership; it does not imply shorter lifetime or lower peak memory.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Vectorization, SIMD, code generation, fusion, and columnar storage are not treated as equivalent mechanisms.

evidence: Reviewed empty/all-null/no-null batches, bitmap slices, sparse/reordered selections, dictionary chains, constant/lazy values, and nested offsets.
Reviewed lane tails, unaligned buffers, overflow, decimal rounding, NaN/signed zero, division errors, huge strings, and output expansion.
Reviewed decompression amplification, native/off-heap retention, UDF ownership, worker ISA mismatch, spill/exchange corruption, retry, and cancellation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Semantic, memory, representation, compatibility, distributed failure, and resource boundaries are reviewed separately.

evidence: Traced schema/vector/buffer identity through storage decode, filter/project, join, aggregate, exchange, spill, UDF, and output.
Checked length, validity, selection, encoding, offset/child, ownership, mutability, lifetime, and accounting invariants.
Checked worker capability negotiation, scalar fallback, backpressure, attempt identity, retries, and output commit preserve semantics.
invariant_checking.notes: Borrowed, shared, transferred, materialized, serialized, spilled, and released buffers remain distinct states.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from scalar semantics and vector contracts through kernels, boundaries, memory, retries, telemetry, and testing.
Checked selection and batch-partition equivalence arguments and their ordering/state/effect premises.
Checked zero-copy qualification and why buffer reuse alone is not an end-to-end performance proof.
proof_review.notes: Correctness, memory safety, compatibility, throughput, latency, fairness, and cost remain separate claims.

evidence: Audited vectorized, SIMD, generated, fused, flat, constant, dictionary, lazy, selected, compacted, borrowed, and zero-copy terminology.
Confirmed logical nullness is not inferred from payload and dictionary indices are not mislabeled values.
Confirmed wire/encoded/compressed/decoded/live/shared/native/device representations remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every optimization label identifies its layer and ownership/semantic boundary.

evidence: Reviewed rows/active positions/batches, logical/physical bytes, null/selectivity, copies/materialization, decode, memory, CPU, stalls, backpressure, fallback, tails, energy, and cost.
Confirmed no universal batch rows/bytes, lane width, credit, cache size, fusion, fallback, spill, or adaptation threshold is prescribed.
Confirmed production acceptance requires scalar/vector differential tests, representation fuzzing, sanitizers, failure injection, realistic concurrency benchmarks, canary, freeze, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Micro-level throughput is not mislabeled cluster-level success.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed execution techniques, vector contracts, validity/selections, encodings, variable/nested data, batch/cache/SIMD/fusion, operators, storage, exchange, spill, language/UDF boundaries, heterogeneous workers, memory, backpressure, adaptation, observability, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable schema/buffer contracts, bounds validation, ownership callbacks, encoding dispatch, byte-aware batching, output-expansion resumability, decoded-credit accounting, native memory attribution, capability negotiation, causal telemetry, fuzzing, canary, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from representation and semantics to cluster boundaries and evaluation. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover validity, bitmap slices, selections, dictionaries, batch memory, SIMD tails, join expansion, decompression, UDF ownership, executable selection, nested contracts, differential testing, batch policy, zero-copy, and production evaluation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Arrow/DuckDB/DataFusion/Spark/ORC/Parquet/Velox maintainer, Dremel/F1 researcher, query-engine operator, compiler/CPU/memory-safety/distributed-systems/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
